title.title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
title.subtitle: Claim: for large primes, a spectrum of fp-type 2 is not finitely built from $\mathrm{BP}\langle 2\rangle$

plain: A shape that passes every finiteness test, yet can't be built from the standard bricks in finitely many steps

beats.text: fp-type 2: mod-$p$ cohomology finitely presented over the Steenrod algebra
Hahn–Wilson predicted every such spectrum is finitely built from $\mathrm{BP}\langle 2\rangle$
Claimed: a spectrum $X$ outside, for every large prime (schematically)

steps: Glue standard pieces along an operator with many independent defects
Show no finite run of sums, shifts and cones can produce the result

achievement.label: Hahn–Wilson conjecture at height 2
achievement.context: Yet $L_2^f X = L_2 X$ and $L_{T(2)} X = L_{K(2)} X$: both telescope comparisons hold
achievement.note: Only for sufficiently large $p$, against a specified form of $\mathrm{BP}\langle 2\rangle$

verify.detail: Manuscript only: 79 pages, a technical result
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Every spectrum of this type was predicted to be finitely built from the standard bricks.
Glue bricks along an operator with many defects; no finite build reaches it.
Claimed: true for every large prime.

sources.quote: For every sufficiently large prime p there is a connective p-complete spectrum X of exact fp-type 2 not in the thick subcategory generated by (a specified standard form of) BP<2>^_p, although L_2^f X = L_2 X and L_{T(2)}X = L_{K(2)}X; refuting the Hahn-Wilson conjecture at height 2.
Only 'sufficiently large p'; depends on 'the specified standard form' of BP<2>. 79 pages.
fp-type spectra are those whose mod-p cohomology is finitely presented over the Steenrod algebra
